title: Rav Sherevia
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a student of Abaye and of Rava, as in Bava Metzia 64 and Bekhorot 19a, where he raised a difficulty against Abaye and Abaye resolved his difficulty for him.

And in Shabbat 136b: Ravina said in the name of Rava, and Rav Sherevia said in the name of Rava— Ravina said to him, “In the evening Rava said thus; in the morning he retracted.” He said to him, “Have you all permitted it? May it be [God’s] will that you all permit fat.”
Hyman cites Yevamot 102a for his challenge to Rava from a baraita; he said to him, "If it was taught, it was taught."
He is mentioned in Pesachim 98a resolving the words of the baraita after Abaye.
And in Yevamot 53a he resolves the baraita after Rava, and Hyman includes there at 71a: Rav Shemaya said: to include a circumcised Arab.
And in Zevachim 58b he said: Whose view is this? It is that of Rabbi Yose the Galilean.
And in Yoma 13b Ravina objected to it, and some say Rav Sherevia.
And in Kiddushin 9b, [regarding a document] written for her sake but without her knowledge: Rava and Ravina say—R' Pappa and Rav Sherevia say she is not betrothed.
Hyman describes him as a judge in his town, from which he sent his queries to Abaye, as in Bava Batra 166b.
And we find Rav bar Sherevia in Shevuot 30b.

notes.text: The named Yevamot71a passage reads Rav Shemaya, not Rav Sherevia; Hyman includes it in this notice, and that attribution remains a substantive question. Zevachim58b spells out Rabbi Yose the Galilean, resolving ר״יהג. All dates and Rav bar Sherevia’s separate occurrence remain as supplied.

Three whole saved Davidson digital scalars were read with raw SHA256, selectors, scalar hashes and actual edition metadata checked: Yevamot53a versions[0].text[1] (287 characters), Yevamot71a versions[0].text[9] (132 characters), and legacy Zevachim58b he[15] (199 characters). The first explicitly names Rav Sherevia; the second explicitly names Rav Shemaya, as does Hyman's supplied line. Neither authorizes changing Shemaya to Sherevia or explaining why the line occurs in this notice. The search return's Shemaya-only result is a bounded historical report, not a new search or proof that no variant exists. The separate 71b Sherevia observation is not a repair; Dikdukei Soferim has not been collated here. Its incomplete closing verse fragment is not imported or completed. Every explicit full Rav remains, including the heading, Shemaya and the separate Rav bar Sherevia occurrence. Ravina, Abaye and Rava remain proper names without added titles; abbreviated R-P is contextually Pappa with R' retained, without transfer of a full title from another passage. The heading's biblical Sherevia/Nehemiah9:4 parallel is not an identity. Hyman's student, judge, town and reporting claims are translated as source claims without authority, chronology or genealogy admission. Bava Metzia64 remains unsided. The Shabbat exchange preserves the plural Have you all permitted it and May it be God's will that you all permit fat, with God's as a disclosed contextual supplement; the abbreviated speakers are not independently identified or reconciled. The earlier Shabbat136b note is retained as historical comparison, not newly inspected whole-primary evidence. No missing first Kiddushin opinion, extra circumcised Gibeonite, Rabbi Akiva context, legal sequel or scripture is imported. All original mixed notes, current note, carried notes, original responses and historical English remain exact, with this qualification appended. Source hold p006 remains.

The printed notice (volume III, p. 1230) itself says Rav Shemaya at Yevamot 71a, as does the consulted passage. Why Hyman includes that occurrence here remains unresolved; it does not establish that Shemaya and Sherevia are one person or that a copyist made a particular error. The same printed notice gives Yevamot 102a for “If it was taught, it was taught.” The directly consulted named exchange is at Yevamot 112a: both parties admit that the levirate marriage was not consummated, Rava proposes chalitzah, Sherevia cites a baraita requiring a bill of divorce and chalitzah, and Rava accepts the objection. Hyman’s supplied 102a is retained and explicitly distinguished from that direct locus. The whole Shabbat 136b exchange confirms the evening/morning contrast and the plural rebuke about permitting fat; its omitted opening law is not added to Hyman’s dash. Zevachim 58b names Rabbi Yose the Galilean. Kiddushin 9b states the affirmative view of Rava and Ravina before the negative view of Rav Pappa and Sherevia, but Hyman’s omission of the first ruling is not silently filled. Bava Batra 166b directly has Sherevia send a monetary-document question to Abaye; it does not independently establish Hyman’s claim that he was a judge in his own town. Hyman’s student and judgeship descriptions remain attributed claims. The separate Rav bar Sherevia notice is not merged with this figure. Exact Dikdukei Soferim readings and other uninspected passages remain uncollated; earlier notes retain their historical inspection limits.
